title: All Four Iraqi Airports Suspend Iranian Flights Under New US Aviation Sanctions
detail: Najaf, Erbil and Sulaimaniya joined Baghdad on September 25 in suspending Iranian carrier flights, closing every major Iraqi airport to Iranian airlines. The move enforces new US sanctions, announced to take effect September 23, targeting any company doing business with Iranian airlines in an effort to ground Iran's civilian fleet worldwide; Iran had already cancelled its own Tehran-Baghdad and Tehran-Muscat flights ahead of the deadline. An Iraqi airline employee at Najaf airport told AFP that Iranian carriers normally operated at least 20 daily flights, but only four remained scheduled after the suspension. Iran's Civil Aviation Authority separately ordered all domestic airlines to stop selling tickets for flights to Iraq, and senior Iranian officials threatened retaliation against neighboring countries' airports that cooperate with the US campaign.

media.caption: Iraqi airports halt Iranian carrier flights after new US aviation sanctions take effect

title: US Hands Over Diplomatic Support Centre at Baghdad Airport to Iraq
detail: US Charge d'Affaires Steven Fagin and Iraqi Deputy Foreign Minister Mohammed Hussein Bahr al-Uloom signed an agreement transferring the Diplomatic Support Centre at Baghdad International Airport to the Iraqi government, days ahead of the September 30 deadline for full US-led coalition withdrawal. The facility, originally part of the US Victory Base military installation, was repurposed as a diplomatic and logistics hub during the 2011 troop withdrawal and has faced repeated drone and rocket attacks since the US-Iran war began in February 2026. Bahr al-Uloom said the handover was 'transitioning a new phase of co-operation and partnership in a number of areas of mutual interest.'

media.caption: The US and Iraq sign a deal transferring the Diplomatic Support Centre at Baghdad airport to Iraqi control

title: Zaidi Pitches 'Invest With Iraq' Economic Vision at UN General Assembly
detail: PM Ali al-Zaidi told the UN General Assembly on September 25: 'Here from the United Nations we say to the world: invest with Iraq. Iraq has resources, markets, a good location and the necessary will to build a new economy.' He said Iraq wants to develop energy links with Turkey, Jordan and Syria to help address the Strait of Hormuz bottleneck, and described efforts to strengthen Iraq's borders and expand state authority to prevent security vulnerabilities that extremist groups could exploit. Zaidi also called for a sovereign Palestinian state, saying there can be no regional stability without a just resolution, and positioned Iraq as a bridge for regional dialogue and cooperation.

media.caption: PM Ali al-Zaidi appeals for investment in Iraq during his UN General Assembly address
